header.running_head: Dhikr of (سُبْحَانَ اللّٰهِ) ('Subhaanallaah'), (اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ) ('Al Hamdulillaah'), (لَا اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اللّٰهُ) ('Laa Ilaaha Illallaah'), (اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ) ('Allaahu Akbar') and (لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ) ('Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illa Billaah')

blocks.text: taken on the journey of Mi'raaj, he passed by Hadhrat Ibraheem (AS), who asked, "Who is this with you, O Jibra'eel (AS)?" "This is Muhammad ﷺ," Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) replied. Hadhrat Ibraheem (AS) then said, "O Muhammad ﷺ! Inform your Ummah to acquire the plants of Jannah in abundance because the soil of Jannah is extremely fertile and its land is very vast." "What are the plants of Jannah?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. Hadhrat Ibraheem (AS) replied, "(لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ) ('Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illa Billaah')." [^1] Another adds that before addressing Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Ibraheem (AS) first greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ and welcomed him. [^2]

The Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) about (لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ) ('Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illa Billaah') and what Hadhrat Imraan (RA) had to say about the Virtues of Praising Allaah

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Whoever says (بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ) ('Bismillaah') has thought of Allaah, whoever says (اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ) ('Al Hamdulillaah') has thanked Allaah, whoever says (اَللّٰهُ اَكْبَرُ) ('Allaahu Akbar') has revered Allaah, whoever says (لَا اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اللّٰهُ) ('Laa Ilaaha Illallaah') has expressed the oneness of Allaah and whoever says (لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ اِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ) ('Laa Howla wa Laa Quwwata Illa Billaah') has submitted himself to Allaah and these words will be an adornment and a treasure for him in Jannah." [^3]

Hadhrat Mutarraf reports that Hadhrat Imraan (RA) once said to him, "Should I not inform you of a Hadith today which Allaah will make a source of benefit for you even after this day? You should note that the best of Allaah's bondsmen on the Day of Qiyaamah shall be those who praised Him most excessively." [^4]
Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s Explanation of the Terms (اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ) ('Al Hamdulillaah') and (سُبْحَانَ اللّٰهِ) ('Subhaanallaah')

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "While we know what is meant by (سُبْحَانَ اللّٰهِ) ('Subhaanallaah') and (لَا اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اللّٰهُ) ('Laa Ilaaha Illallaah'), what is (اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ) ('Al Hamdulillaah')?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied by saying, "It is a phrase that Allaah chose for Himself and which He loves that it be said." [^5]
Hadhrat Abu Dhabyaan narrates that Ibn Kawwaa once asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) about the phrase (سُبْحَانَ اللّٰهِ) ('Subhaanallaah'), to which Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied,
